ParameterSetMetaModel.description: Parameter set metadata: the name documents use in `meta.params`.

name.description: Unique parameter set name, named in a document's meta.params

labels.description: Optional labels (key-value pairs for classification/filtering). A label such as role: spoke is only for attributeconfig selectors: the role a set's values are read under comes from the meta.params of the document that names it.

tags.description: Optional tags (list of values for categorization)

ParameterSetSpecModel.description:
Parameter set specification: the values themselves.

Rules:
- values holds plain YAML only: no ${...} token in any key or value. Write $${...} for the literal text.
- A parameter set is plain text in git: never put a secret in it. Read secrets with ${secret:} in the document's spec instead.

values.description: The values: a map of any YAML (scalars, lists and nested maps). A document that names this set under a role in meta.params reads them with ${param:<role>.<key>}; nested maps are walked with dots (${param:spoke.network.cidr}). No ${...} tokens: values are plain.

description: One named set of plain values: the instance data of a spoke, a hub, a customer or a tenant. A deployment, environment or tenant names it under a role in `meta.params`, and its base reads the values with `${param:<role>.<key>}`, so one base serves many instances.

apiVersion.description: API version for parameter set configuration

meta.description: Parameter set metadata (name, annotations, labels, tags)

spec.description:
Parameter set specification (the values)

Rules:
- values holds plain YAML only: no ${...} token in any key or value. Write $${...} for the literal text.
- A parameter set is plain text in git: never put a secret in it. Read secrets with ${secret:} in the document's spec instead.
